messages:
maya: Quick heads-up — during the 5% canary for model v3.2-int4 we saw a small but consistent MRR drop on the short-answer slice (~1.6%) and a +2.8% uptick in hallucination rate on the longform test set. dashboard: https://rwd/dash/condense?run=canary-1767

maya: Can we define an autofallback policy for this bring-up? I want rules that are precise enough to avoid noisy rollbacks but strict enough to stop bad pushes. Thinking: MRR delta threshold, hallucination spike, and latency tail increase. Thoughts? :thinking_face:

devin: agree. my baseline proposal:
- immediate rollback if MRR drop >= 2.0% on any critical slice (short-answer, api-summaries)
- OR hallucination-rate increase >= 3.0% overall
- OR p95 latency increase >= 100ms

devin: also require the signal to be sustained for at least 5 minutes (rolling window) before triggering

sriram: +1 but add concordance check vs shadow baseline. if concordance falls by >= 2.5% on the reserved concordance set => rollback. that helps catch quality regressions that don't show in MRR alone.

joel: nit: use a two-tier trigger: soft-fail (auto-throttle) vs hard-rollback. for soft-fail we drop traffic by half and run an immediate expanded smoke eval. hard-rollback only if the expanded eval confirms the regression. prevents oscillation.

ana: (typo: ana) i'd add a latency SLO guard: p95 increase > 50ms should first trigger a cooldown (no more than 10% traffic bump) before rollback. some quant variants increase CPU latency sporadically during kv-cache misses.

maya: good points. propose we encode like this config snippet (candidate):

```yaml
policy_name: liftwatch-v3-int4
canary: 5% for 30m -> 25% for 2h -> promote
triggers:
  - name: mrr_drop
    slicer: [short-answer, api-summaries]
    comparator: relative
    threshold: -0.015  # 1.5%
    window: 300       # 5 min
    action: hard-rollback
  - name: hallucination_rate
    comparator: relative
    threshold: 0.03   # +3%
    window: 300
    action: hard-rollback
  - name: concordance_reserved
    comparator: relative
    threshold: -0.02  # 2%
    window: 600       # 10 min
    action: auto-throttle
  - name: p95_latency
    comparator: absolute
    threshold: 50      # ms
    window: 300
    action: cooldown
```

maya: Does everyone feel 1.5% vs 2% is the right line? I want to be a bit conservative because this is a performance-optimized quantized variant.

devin: 1.5% makes sense for the first canary stage. we can tighten to 1.0% when we move to 25% traffic. also add: require at least N=2000 requests in the window or else ignore (avoid tiny-sample noise).

sriram: agree on sample floor. also log a snapshot payload for any trigger so we can reproduce in eval harness: include prompt, seed, kv-hit flag. makes postmortems much faster.

joel: also add a hysteresis to avoid flip-flop: once throttled/rolled-back, block re-promotes for 24h unless manual override.

deploy-bot: started canary: model=v3.2-int4 variant=quant-bridge traffic=5% started_at=1767899991

ops-bot: telemetry note — p95 latency on canary nodes spiked +62ms at 1767900002 (kv cache refill event). correlates with the longform hallucination uptick window.

maya: thanks. i'll update the policy with N floor and hysteresis, and open a PR with the yaml + smoke eval script and the reserved concordance set. i'll also add the snapshot logging snippet sriram asked for.

devin: command to apply once PR is approved:
`rwdctl rollout apply --policy liftwatch-v3-int4 --env canary`

ana: please add a metric in Console for 'auto-fallback_count' so product/SEs can see how often these fire.

maya: will do. i'll ping when PR is up. if anyone wants to bend thresholds before i cut the PR speak now (30m). :white_check_mark:

joel: +1. will review in ~15m.

maya: thanks — keeping this thread as the policy TODO and action list.
